heading.en: Why do we have to choose?

hook.en: You have ₹500 for the month. A new pen drive, a movie ticket and a gift for your sister all cost ₹300 each. Which will you buy?

say.en: You have 500 rupees for the month. A new pen drive, a movie ticket and a gift for your sister all cost 300 rupees each. Which will you buy? In this lesson: Explain scarcity and choice.
Name the three economic activities.
Tell economic from non-economic activities.

body.en: Human wants are unlimited, but the resources to satisfy them (money, land, labour, time) are limited. Because of this *scarcity* we must choose which wants to satisfy first. Economics studies how people and societies make these choices.
body.kn: ಮಾನವನ ಬಯಕೆಗಳು ಅಪರಿಮಿತ, ಆದರೆ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳು ಸೀಮಿತ. ಈ ಕೊರತೆಯಿಂದಾಗಿ ನಾವು ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಅರ್ಥಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ ಈ ಆಯ್ಕೆಗಳ ಅಧ್ಯಯನ.

title.en: Who does what in an economy?

prompt.en: Sort each person by their economic role in the example.

text.en: A farmer growing rice to sell
A potter making pots for the market
A family buying vegetables for dinner

explanation.en: Producers make goods or services for sale, consumers buy them to satisfy wants, and service holders work for others for a wage or salary. One person can play different roles at different times.

body.en: A consumer buys goods and services to satisfy wants. A producer makes goods or services for sale. Service holders work for others for a wage or salary. The three main economic activities are production, consumption and *distribution*. Activities done for money are economic; those done out of love or social duty are non-economic.
body.kn: ಗ್ರಾಹಕ ಬಯಕೆ ತೀರಿಸಲು ಸರಕು ಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಉತ್ಪಾದಕ ಮಾರಾಟಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ, ಅನುಭೋಗ ಮತ್ತು ವಿತರಣೆ ಮುಖ್ಯ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Classify each activity as economic or non-economic: a a doctor treating patients in a clinic, b the same doctor treating her own child at home, c a student doing a part-time delivery job.
a The doctor earns fees: economic.
b No payment; done out of love: non-economic.
c The student earns wages: economic.
So the answer is a economic, b non-economic, c economic.
